title: Low-latency streaming pipeline for Console metrics (queue + stream processors)
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: The Console needs sub-5s visibility into route-level metrics (latency, errors, token volume, concurrency) for live dashboards and alerts. Current batch ETL (5–15 minute ingestion into analytics tables) produces stale dashboards and delayed alerts during incidents.

This ticket scopes building a production-grade real-time streaming pipeline: producers -> durable queue -> stream processors -> low-latency materialized stores + long-term archival. The pipeline should be fault-tolerant, support schema evolution, tenant isolation, replay, and allow efficient aggregation windows per tenant and route.

Goals: Provide 99.9% availability of fresh metrics, 95th percentile end-to-end latency < 3s for aggregated dashboards, and safe rollouts with replay and backfill capabilities.

Out of scope: Rewriting individual Console pages or changing frontend charts; those will consume the new metrics once stable endpoints are available.
acceptance_criteria: Console dashboards reflect aggregated metric windows (1s/10s/1m) with end-to-end latency <= 3s P95 during 90th percentile load
Producer libraries added to Console backend with feature-flagged publish to console.metrics.v1 topic and schema validated against Schema Registry
Stateless stream processors deployed (Flink/Kafka Streams) computing per-tenant per-route aggregates and writing to ClickHouse low-latency table
Raw events sinked to S3 (compressed, partitioned by date) via Kafka Connect for audit and backfill
Canary rollout and fallback plan tested: ability to switch consumers to batch pipeline within 15 minutes
Instrumentation and dashboards for pipeline health: topic lag, processor throughput, processing latency, error rates, and consumer lag alerts
implementation_notes:
Design overview: producers (Console API + ingestion lambdas) will emit Protobuf telemetry events to Kafka topic console.metrics.v1. Use Confluent Schema Registry (or equivalent) to manage schemas and enforce compatibility. Stream processors implemented in Flink (preferred for windowing semantics) will perform tenant-aware aggregations (sliding windows: 1s, 10s, 1m) and write results into ClickHouse via a durable HTTP bulk insert or native ClickHouse sink. Raw event retention: topic retention 72 hours, Kafka Connect S3 sink writes raw events to s3://redwood-console-metrics/raw/YYYY/MM/DD/HH/*.parquet for 30-day archival.

Exactly-once vs at-least-once: We'll aim for end-to-end effectively-once for aggregates using Flink checkpoints and idempotent ClickHouse writes (dedupe keys windows). For initial rollout we may accept at-least-once but include dedupe TTL on materialized rows.

Schema: event fields include tenant_id, route_id, request_id, timestamp_ms, latency_ms, status_code, token_count, model, instance_id, flags. Keep event size small to minimize cost.

Operational concerns: topic partitioning by tenant_id hash + route to avoid hot tenants. Provision partitions based on high-percentile tenant load. Implement fine-grained RBAC for write access to topics and S3 buckets. Add quotas per-tenant at producer level.

Storage: ClickHouse for low-latency aggregated reads + object storage for raw event archival. For low-cardinality real-time counters (active_concurrency) we will also write to Redis Streams (or in-memory store) with TTL to power some live widgets.

Testing strategy: unit tests for topology, integration tests with local Kafka + Flink harness, canary on dev cluster with synthetic high-volume load, then staging with shadow traffic. Include data drift/regression fuzz tests against existing batch metrics to ensure numerical parity within acceptable bounds.

Rollout: 1) Create topics and schemas, 2) deploy producers behind feature flag, 3) deploy processors in dev, run shadowing, 4) canary on 5% of requests -> validate, 5) incrementally ramp to 100%, 6) deprecate batch consumers after 2-week parity window.
tasks: Create Kafka topic console.metrics.v1 with partition plan and ACLs (ENG-8801 dependency)
Add producer instrumentation library to console-backend and feature-flag publish
Build Flink job for multi-window aggregation + per-tenant partitioning
Implement ClickHouse sink and Idempotent writes strategy
Configure Kafka Connect S3 sink for raw archival
Add Redis Streams for live counters (optional for widgets)
End-to-end test harness and load test (k6 or custom tool)
Create dashboards and alerts for topic lag, processor latency, failed events
Run canary, validate parity, and do incremental ramp
